name: Gaigel
description: Gaigel is a traditional trick-taking game hailing from Swabia in Southwest Germany. Closely related to the game 'Sixty-Six' (Sechsundsechzig), Gaigel is played with a double-deck of 48 cards, typically featuring the distinct German-suited WÃ¼rttemberg pattern. It is primarily a partnership game where the goal is to reach 101 card points through captured tricks and 'marriages' (King and Ober pairs). The game is famous for its midndgame shift, where strict following-suit rules only apply once the draw pile (Talon) is exhausted.

content.text: Gaigel is a traditional trick-taking game hailing from Swabia in Southwest Germany. Closely related to the game 'Sixty-Six' (Sechsundsechzig), Gaigel is played with a double-deck of 48 cards, typically featuring the distinct German-suited WÃ¼rttemberg pattern. It is primarily a partnership game where the goal is to reach 101 card points through captured tricks and 'marriages' (King and Ober pairs). The game is famous for its midndgame shift, where strict following-suit rules only apply once the draw pile (Talon) is exhausted.

Gaigel originated in the 19th century in the Swabian region of Germany. It is named after its highest rank (the 'Gaigel' or Ace in some dialects). It co-evolved with Binokel and represents a rich tradition of Southwestern German pub games.
4 players in two partnerships (North/South vs East/West).
48 cards (WÃ¼rttemberg pattern). Two copies of Ace, 10, King, Ober, Unter, and 7 per suit.

items.text: Six-Player Partnership: Uses the same core rules with three-player teams seated opposite each other; the talon is exhausted much earlier.
Five Sevens: Some tables allow a player with five sevens to claim an immediate single game win for their side.
Auf Siebener: A player with four sevens may announce and attempt to draw the fifth from talon before opponents reach 101.
